title: Protocol for assessing ex vivo lipolysis of murine adipose tissue
protocol: Dissect subcutaneous (inguinal) and visceral (perigonadal) white fat pads from adult C57BL/6J mice.
Position the mouse ventral side up.
Make a skin incision to expose the subcutaneous adipose tissue depots bilaterally beside the skeletal muscle.
Identify the base of the major artery connecting the adipose tissue and make a superficial cut into the tissue.
Dissect the peritoneal layer of the C57BL/6J mouse for eWAT extraction.
Locate the eWAT in male mice with respect to the gonads.
Locate the eWAT in female mice with respect to the uterus.
Euthanize mouse – Follow general CO2 euthanasia procedure in accordance with Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee approval.
Spray 8-9 week-old C57BL/6J mouse ventral side up with 70% ethanol.
Make a longitudinal midline incision from the base of the tail to top of the sternum carefully avoiding the peritoneal cavity.
Make lateral incisions on either side of the midline at the top of the sternum and pull the skin apart using anatomical forceps or thumb.
Pin the exposed adipose tissue to the dissection base once it is visible.
Hold the edge of the subcutaneous adipose depot with anatomical forceps.
Cut superficially at the base of the large vessel joining the tissue, then cut along the tissue boundaries.
Gently pull the subcutaneous adipose tissue away from the skin and tap it on a Kimwipe to drain interstitial fluid.
Weigh the detached subcutaneous fat depot using a precision scale.
Excise visceral white adipose tissue depot.
Make a midline Y-shaped incision in the peritoneal cavity to expose the visceral organs.
Hold and cut the tissue along the anterior edge of the gonads or uterus using anatomical forceps.
Repeat step 2f following dissection.
Set up the assay plate for glycerol and fatty acid release after tissue dissections.
Incubate the tube in a laboratory oven or CO2 incubator as described in step 1 of ‘before you begin’.
Transfer whole iWAT (∼350–500 mg) or eWAT (∼150–400 mg) adipose tissue into 15-mL centrifuge tubes containing 5 mL of pre-warmed KRBH buffer (w/o 2% BSA), pH 7.4.
Cut 50 mg of adipose tissue and place it into one well of a 24-well plate containing 1 mL of pre-warmed KRBH buffer with 2% fatty acid free BSA (KRBH-BSA buffer).
Incubate the plate in a laboratory oven at 37°C.
Aspirate the medium from each well of the plate and replenish with KRBH-BSA buffer containing either vehicle (CTR) or isoproterenol (10 μM).
Collect 100 μL of medium as a baseline after 5 minutes.
Replenish each well with 100 μL of respective medium (with vehicle or isoproterenol).
Incubate the plate for 2 hours at 37°C.
Collect a 1 mL aliquot of the incubation medium after 2 hours.
Incubate baseline and 2 hour media aliquots at 65°C for 10 minutes to overcome residual enzymatic action.
Wash tissue chunks in the 24-well plate using 1 mL of 1× PBS.
Store washed tissue at -80°C after discarding PBS.
Set up the reaction plate close to the incubator or oven to minimize time loss during dissection and incubation.
Thaw samples stored at -80°C and glycerol reagent stored at -20°C at 20°C-25°C for 30 min protected from light.
Prepare a range of glycerol standards in distilled (d)H2O.
Run a trial assay to determine if the glycerol levels are within the standard range of the assay and adjust the standard range if required.
Add 50 μl of either sample or standard plus 100 μl of the glycerol reagent in duplicates to a clear 96-well plate.
Mix well by shaking on a horizontal shaker for 15 s.
Cover the plate using aluminum foil.
Incubate for 15 min at 20°C-25°C.
Collect absorbance at 540 nm using a standard UV-visible spectrophotometric plate reader capable of end-point absorbance analysis.
Thaw samples following step 6.
Prepare a range of standards.
Dilute the palmitic acid stock solution to 10 times using the assay buffer provided in the kit in a 1.5-mL centrifuge tube to create a 0.1 nmol/μl standard solution.
In a black solid bottom 96-well plate, add 0, 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 μl of the diluted standard solution to generate a 0.2–1 nmol/well concentration range.
Wrap the tube using aluminum foil to protect it from light at all times.
Dilute samples 1:1 using the assay buffer (e.g., 50 μL sample + 50 μL assay buffer).
Add 5 μL of the diluted sample to the plate.
For standards, add 50, 48, 46, 44, 42 and 40 μL of assay buffer.
For samples, add 45 μL of assay buffer to bring the final volume to 50 μL.
Add 2 μL of ACS reagent (Acetyl CoA Synthetase enzyme mix) to each well of sample and standard solutions.
Incubate for 30 min at 37°C.
Mix well by shaking on a horizontal shaker for 15 s.
Cover the plate using aluminum foil.
Calculate the amount of master mix required based on sample number and technical replicates.
Prepare the master mix accordingly.
To 50 μL of either sample or standard, add 50 μL of the master mix in duplicate.
Cover the plate using aluminum foil to prevent light exposure.
Mix well by shaking on a horizontal rocker for 15 s.
Incubate for 30 min at 37°C.
Measure fluorescence intensity at an excitation maximum of 535 nm and an emission maximum of 590 nm using a multimode plate reader that can measure fluorescence intensity under standard conditions.
Thaw 24-well plate containing adipose tissue samples on ice for 30 min.
Transfer tissue samples into labeled and pre-chilled DNAse-RNAse free Lysing Matrix D tubes with zirconium beads of 1.4 mm diameter.
Add six volumes of ice-cold lysis buffer supplemented with protease and phosphate inhibitor to each sample.
Homogenize the samples in a bullet blender homogenizer for 5 min at maximum speed.
Transfer the tissue homogenate to clean pre-chilled 1.5-mL tubes.
Centrifuge the samples at 13,523 g for 15 min at 4°C.
Using a 23-gauge needle or gel-loading fine tip, carefully penetrate the fat layer and collect the aqueous supernatant.
Transfer the collected supernatant into clean pre-chilled 1.5-mL tubes.
Incubate on ice for 30 min.
Sonicate the samples for 10 s using a hand-held sonicator set at 80% amplitude.
Centrifuge at 13,523 g for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Transfer the aqueous supernatant into clean pre-chilled 1.5-mL tubes.
Repeat centrifugation and transfer steps two more times to maximize extraction of lipid content.
Store samples at -80°C until protein estimation.
Thaw samples on ice for 20 minutes.
Dilute samples tenfold using distilled water.
Add 5 μL of diluted sample to 200 μL of BCA reagent mix.
Incubate the samples at 37°C for 30 minutes.
Measure absorbance at 562 nm.
Calculate protein concentration in lysates against a BSA standard (0–2 mg/mL).
Evaluate glycerol levels in the samples by measuring absorbance at 540 nm using a standard UV-visible spectrophotometric plate reader.
Extrapolate the glycerol concentration using the standard plot that was generated in step 10.
Normalize the value to the respective protein concentration of the sample.
Express glycerol levels as μg/mL glycerol per mg of protein.

Evaluate fatty acid levels in the samples by measuring fluorescence intensity at an excitation maximum of 535 nm and an emission maximum of 590 nm using a multimode plate reader that can measure fluorescence intensity under standard conditions.
Extrapolate the fatty acid concentration using the standard plot that was generated in step 14.
Multiply the fatty acid concentration by two (dilution factor, as the sample was originally diluted to half).
Divide the value by five (5 μL is sample volume/well).
Normalize the value from step 20c to the respective protein concentration of the sample.
Express free fatty acid levels as nmol/mg protein.
Treat additional iWAT or eWAT with vehicle (CTR) or insulin in KRBH-BSA buffer for 2 hours at 37°C.
Collect treated adipose tissue and homogenize it as described.
Fractionate a portion of the lysate by SDS-polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis.
Transfer proteins to a nitrocellulose membrane using 300 mAmp for 3 h.
Stain the membrane with Ponceau S to confirm equal loading and transfer.
Block the membrane at 20°C–25°C with 5% nonfat milk in TBST for 1 hour.
Probe the membrane with a rabbit monoclonal anti-phospho-Akt (Ser473).
Use a rabbit monoclonal anti-Akt (pan) for protein-loading control.
